name: Hellfire X

tenures.role: owner — the fed’s own in-card Owner, and a wrestler on its 2003 roster
tenures.source: his own info card (promotions/cwf/archive/hellfire-x-info-card.html) and biography (promotions/cwf/archive/hellfire-x-biography.html); the fed’s own History, In-Card Staff and Real Staff pages
tenures.note: His own biography claims better than sixty federations, a first world title won in a War of Independence match, and a manager he was engaged to marry. The 1998 start date is the fed’s own History page, which names him one of its three founders; the last document that names him is a May 2003 capture of his own info card.

caption: Founded the Corporate Wrestling Federation in 1998, restarted it twice, walked to the ring first on the night it came back for the third time, and announced his own last e-fed match three months later.

name: Sean Manning

tenures.role: wrestler — opened CWF SeVeN against Xtreme Max
tenures.source: his own bio card (promotions/cwf/archive/sean-manning-bio-card.html); the fed’s own roster and Top Ten
tenures.note: His bio card is by some distance the longest document CWF left about a single wrestler — a childhood in West Side Los Angeles told at length through the woman who raised him, a school expulsion, a revenge killing and three years in juvenile detention before he trained for wrestling. The card’s own entrance description is reused word for word in the SeVeN script.

caption: Came out of a bio card that runs to eleven thousand words of orphanhood, revenge and juvenile detention, and opened CWF SeVeN with a snap suplex.

name: Kid Gangster

name: Dax

tenures.role: authority-figure — website builder and later co-owner across the fed's original run, CEO of a later fed called HATE, restarted CWF with Hellfire X in January 2003 before leaving within a week, then returned in April 2003 to run the fed's own management-applications drive after Hellfire X's own departure
tenures.source: the fed's own History page, which also names him Rattlesnake/Justin-X-Treme (promotions/cwf/archive/history.html); the Redz()ne-1 reunion show, where his own invitation is revoked at the door (promotions/cwf/archive/redzone-1-reunion-2003-01-27.html); the 7 and 15 April 2003 headlines, both bylined "By Dax" (promotions/cwf/archive/headlines-2003-04-07.html; promotions/cwf/archive/headlines-2003-04-15.html)
tenures.note: History's own account has him building the original CWF's website, leaving with Hellfire in 2001, running HATE as its absent owner's CEO, and restarting CWF with Hellfire X in January 2003 before leaving "a week after opening" over "unfinished business" — yet the reunion show (27 January) turns him away at the door, and he is the one signing the April 2003 headlines announcing Hellfire X's own departure and the search for new management. The record does not reconcile the two.

caption: Built the original CWF's own website under the name Rattlesnake, ran a later fed called HATE, restarted CWF with Hellfire X in January 2003, and signed the headlines announcing Hellfire X's own departure that April — despite History's own account of him leaving within a week of the restart.
